tags.name: sample_complete_counter
tags.documentation: Demo extension, not the MQTT trigger. The real FLEX2 OPC server has no completion counter at all - SampleResults just changes underneath you. Pattern 3 publishes off result/sample_time (vendor HistoricalSampleResults/SampleTime). This node still increments last in ICC26Extensions so the gap is visible in the address space. A QC run and a failed analysis both leave this untouched. UInt32 on the wire, so Int8 here.

tags.name: qc_complete_counter
tags.documentation: Increments on an onboard QC analysis, which never touches sample_complete_counter. A client watching only sample results silently misses every control run - which is the manual's own warning at the top of section 9.

tags.name: state
tags.documentation: 0 Idle, 1 Running, 2 Completed, 3 Aborted, 4 Error, 5 Calibrating, 6 QualityControl, 7 Maintenance. Also an extension: the vendor publishes no state tag, only ActiveTasks as free text.

tags.name: result_json
tags.documentation: The whole sample result as one JSON document, written in the same transaction as the leaves below. Read this instead of 39 tags when assembling the MQTT payload: it cannot tear across two samples, and it is one OPC read rather than 39.

tags.name: uptime
tags.documentation: Vendor liveness tag. Section 6 of the FLEX2 OPC manual tells you to subscribe to this and to the analyzer clock to confirm the server is updating at all - it is the vendor's own acceptance test, so it is worth having as a tag.

tags.name: esm_schedule_analysis
tags.documentation: Write true to run an analysis. This is the VENDOR's own trigger, not something added for the demo - the FLEX2 exposes no OPC UA methods at all, only writable bits. Set the sample metadata tags below FIRST: nothing here is atomic and the instrument reads them at the instant the bit goes true. There is also no refusal path - write it while an analysis is running and all that happens is nothing.

tags.name: sample_id
tags.documentation: Applied to the NEXT analysis. Read the as-run value back from result/sample_id, never from here - this one is just the request.

tags.name: vessel_temperature
tags.documentation: Degrees C, vendor default 37. The three temperature-corrected calculated results are identities at 37 - change this and watch them separate from their raw twins.

tags.name: esm_terminate
tags.documentation: Aborts a run in progress. State goes to 3 (Aborted) and the counter does not move.

tags.name: gas_qc_level1
tags.documentation: Runs an onboard pH/Gas Level 1 control. Increments qc_complete_counter only.

tags.name: sample_source
tags.documentation: Which sampling path produced this - Manual, ESM, OLS, EXT_OLS.

THE trigger for the MQTT publish. Vendor HistoricalSampleResults/SampleTime, written last by the simulator after every other historical leaf. A valueChanged script hands the result folder to event stream 03_opcua/novaflex-result, which reads the sibling historical tags and publishes via Transmission. Do not point this at ICC26Extensions.
tags.name: sample_time
modified_time
tags.documentation: Not sample_time. Runs later if CDV images are reanalyzed or the result is edited after the fact - so a result CAN change after you have already read it. With no vendor completion counter that is a second reason polling cannot be trusted.

tags.name: errors
tags.documentation: Free text, empty when clean. Per-analyte failures also show up as Bad quality on the individual result tag below - the quality IS the error signal, which is the argument for OPC UA over a CSV that can only write a number.

tags.name: osmo
tags.documentation: The vendor's own absent-vs-zero mechanism, and the reason this folder is worth publishing: False here is Good and true - 'the osmometer did not take part in this analysis' - while result/osmo alongside it is Bad_NoData. Without this a consumer cannot tell 'not measured' from 'lost in transit'.

THE trigger. Monotonic, written last by the instrument after every result field and after state - so when this changes, the whole result branch is settled and consistent. Subscribe to this one tag; do not drive anything off the individual result values. A failed count does NOT increment it. UInt32 on the wire, so Int8 here: it does not fit an Int4.

tags.documentation: 0 Idle, 1 Running, 2 Completed, 3 Aborted, 4 Error. Error and Aborted leave count_completed_counter untouched, which is the point of the counter.

tags.documentation: The protocol the instrument is set to NOW, and writable. result/protocol/name is the one the last count actually ran under - they differ the moment somebody changes protocols between counts.

tags.documentation: The whole result as one JSON document, written in the same transaction as the leaves below. Read this instead of 33 tags when assembling the MQTT payload: it cannot tear across two counts, and it is one OPC read rather than 33.

tags.documentation: Write true to run a new analysis. The instrument clears it back to false as soon as it accepts the request, so this is a one-shot: a client that never resets the bit still gets exactly one count per write. Ignored (and logged) if a count is already running - check state first. Set sample_name before writing this, not after.
tags.name: start_request

tags.documentation: Name applied to the NEXT triggered count. Left empty, the instrument auto-names it SAMPLE-nnnn. Read back the as-run name from result/sample_name, not from here - this one is just the request.
tags.name: sample_name

tags.documentation: Acquisition instant, not write time. Every leaf of a result carries this same SourceTimestamp - that is how you prove a set of reads is one count and not a mixture of two.
tags.name: acquisition_time

tags.documentation: 0 BrightfieldBased, 1 FluorescenceBased. On a 0, every fluorescence tag below goes Bad_NoData - the cube was fitted but not used.

tags.documentation: 0 Brightfield, 1 Fluorescence.

tags.documentation: cells/mL. Instrument range is 1e4 to 1e7 (Appendix B); outside it the value is out of spec, not misscaled.
tags.name: total_concentration

tags.documentation: Trypan-blue viability as the instrument computed it. Derivable from the live/dead counts, but publish this one - a QC record that disagrees with the instrument printout is worse than no record.

tags.documentation: Bad_NoData whenever slot 2 is empty, which is the demo default. Bad is the correct answer here, not 0 - see docs/reference/countess-3fl-opcua-model.md section 8.

tags.documentation: Union of both channels, not their sum - a double-positive cell is counted once. Absent unless both cubes are fitted. Never synthesize this from cube1 + cube2.

tags.documentation: The protocol this count ran under. Compare with the instance-level protocol_name, which is what the instrument is set to now.

eventScripts.script:
# One-shot observer request out to the local vibration gateway.
	# Fires on the rising edge of steady_state && collect_request.
	if initialChange or not currentValue.value:
		return
	
	import sys
	
	# Lines of resolution the gateway accepts: powers of two, 512 .. 4194304.
	LOR_VALUES = [512 << i for i in range(14)]
	
	logger = system.util.getLogger("vibration_sensor.collect")
	base = tagPath.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
	
	topic, gwSerial, channelIndex, resolution = [
		qv.value
		for qv in system.tag.readBlocking([
			base + "/mqtt_topic",
			base + "/gw_serial",
			base + "/channel_index",
			base + "/resolution",
		])
	]
	
	if not topic or not gwSerial or resolution is None:
		logger.warn(
			"collect skipped for %s: mqtt_topic, gw_serial or resolution is unset" % base
		)
		return
	
	# Comes back as a java.lang.Long off an Int8 tag; coerce before the membership test.
	resolution = int(resolution)
	if resolution not in LOR_VALUES:
		logger.warnf(
			"collect skipped for %s: resolution %s is not one of %s",
			base, resolution, LOR_VALUES
		)
		return
	
	payload = {
		"type": "observerrequest",
		"channelIndex": channelIndex,
		"action": "wiredcollectnow",
		"settings": {
			"lor": resolution,
			"sendto": "cloud",
		},
		"gwSerial": gwSerial,
	}
	
	try:
		system.cirruslink.transmission.publish(
			"chariot_broker", topic, system.util.jsonEncode(payload), 1, False
		)
	except:
		logger.error("collect handoff to %s failed" % topic, sys.exc_info()[1])
		return
	
	# publish() neither raises nor returns a status when MQTT Transmission
	# drops the message - it logs its own warning under ClientsManager. So
	# this line means handed to the module, NOT delivered to the broker.
	logger.infof(
		"wiredcollectnow handed to %s for %s ch=%s lor=%s",
		topic, gwSerial, channelIndex, resolution
	)
	
	# Stamp when we asked, then one-shot clear the request so the next collect
	# needs a fresh trigger. This timestamp and the capture time that comes back
	# on the waveform are the whole of this pattern's request/response story -
	# there is no correlation id, because the PM system does not need one.
	system.tag.writeBlocking(
		[base + "/last_request_ts", base + "/collect_request"],
		[system.date.now(), False],
	)

tags.documentation: Gateway serial. Must stay String - undeclared it defaults to numeric and publishes gwSerial unquoted.
tags.name: gw_serial

tags.documentation: When the collect command was handed to MQTT Transmission. Pairs with waveform/captured_at - together they are this pattern's request/response trace, in place of a correlation id.
tags.name: last_request_ts

tags.documentation: Fleet control topic the collect command is published to. Every gateway subscribes to it and self-selects on gwSerial, so this is the same string for every instance; override per instance only if a site runs a separate fleet.

tags.documentation: Lines of resolution sent as settings.lor. Must be a power of two from 512 to 4194304; the collect is rejected otherwise. The simulator caps this at MAX_LOR (65536) - 4096 is ~37 KB on the wire, 32768 is ~300 KB.
